mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2% for 3 consecutive months) signals a potential for monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases over 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter signals a strengthening demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both increase over 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of HOUST and GDPC1 increases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity is abundant and borrowing costs are low.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
